title: St. Louis: Democratic Club and 34 East Market
summary: After the Pelican Handy goes to St. Louis, plays the Democratic Club and 34 East Market, and meets Guy Kelly, Walter Barnes' band and the Jeter-Pillars band.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Yeah, his daddy. Uh-huh. Uh. Well, after I left, uh, Pelican, I left here and went to St. Louis. Worked at the Democratic Club there. Uh-huh. Under a fellow by the name of Hawkins. At the Democratic Club at that time. My Bobby Gordon up there, it was through our, uh, Charlie Chris. Used to work with, with Faith Morgan. He played trumpet and he played, uh, the accordion. Oh. He's dead now, a fellow. Uh, up there I had, uh, I can't remember this guy's name. I don't remember one man's name up there. Was playing with us too. I remember a fellow called Cabbage playing, uh, tenor saxophone. Another boy they called, uh, Bubba, I think they called him. This drummer used to be on the boobah seat. Uh, played at Democratic Club for about 89 months. Maybe, probably a year I played at Democratic Club. And then I left there and went down to 34 East Market. Played a fellow down there, that Italian name, Sam. I played there for, until I got sick. I was there about six months, seven months. Matter of fact, that's the last place I seen Guy Kelly. He was with, uh, uh, Walter Barnes' band. Got burned up in Natchez there. Uh-huh. He was with that band. He come down and stopped in St. Louis there. As a matter of fact, they played somewhere near St. Louis, and on the way back to Chicago, they stopped there. And somebody told them I was at, uh, 34 East Market down there. And they come down there, the whole band come down there. I was playing with a fellow by the name of Joe, Jay Guston, and he was a nice arranger, and he was a piano player. And they had ten pieces in there every night.
That's where I made, met Julius and Pillars out of St. Louis. They were at that, uh, Club Plantation, I think, that's the name of the place they were playing.
